minutes.headline: Cemetery Commission reviewed a draft fiscal policy for cemetery funds and voted to sign three lot-refund approvals for audit.
minutes.summary: The commission heard the finance director's draft fiscal rules for its cemetery accounts and a resident's criticism of its authority. It voted to sign three lot-refund approvals, reorganized with Michael as clerk, and approved two sets of minutes. The Historical Commission chair updated them on lost and family burial plots. The DPW maintenance plan and flag lighting were put on the next agenda.

attendees.role: presenter, chair of Lunenburg Historical Commission

public_comment.topic: Said he has been late getting the commission something it requested and expects to come before it next month.

Criticized the commission's actions, citing the town attorney's letter on the commission's lack of authority over contractor bans and reimbursing the town under chapter 114. He said he is running as a write-in for cemetery commissioner and suggested the commission become a 501c3-style association.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to accept and sign three lot-refund approvals so the finance director can issue the checks.
The finance director presented draft fiscal rules for the cemetery funds and a revenue turnover policy; the draft is to go to the select board.
The commission reorganized for one year: Nancy stays chair, Dave Duran stays vice chair, and Michael becomes clerk.
The DPW annual maintenance plan was tabled, and a vote on lighting the flags at North and South cemeteries goes on the next agenda.
The Historical Commission chair is to have the stone company send an estimate in July for the Goodridge plot wall, with the cemetery commission to supply the stone.

why_it_matters: The draft rules set how lot-sale money, perpetual care interest and gifts are handled, which governs what the town's cemeteries can spend on upkeep and who must be told when a signature is needed.
A gift for the North Cemetery wall cannot enter the gift fund until the project is further along and bid, and the stone for the Goodridge wall is a cost the commission has yet to price.
watch_next: The next meeting was proposed for May 16 at 9 a.m., with members to confirm.
The next agenda is to carry the DPW maintenance plan and the flag illumination vote for North and South cemeteries.
